turns.text: What usually happens after a red day?
turns.intent: No ticker named, so the default (SPY), said. On the session after a day that closed down, what the price typically did (the usual move and path of that next session).
turns.if_asked: SPY. Red day means it closed lower than the day before.
turns.also_fine: Red day read as closing below its own open, if that is said.

turns.text: When does SPY normally make its high?
turns.intent: SPY: at what time of day the session's high is usually made (the distribution of the time of the day's high).
turns.if_asked: The time of day of the day's high, over all the history you have.

turns.text: Does the first hour tell you anything about the rest of the day?
turns.intent: No ticker named, so the default (SPY), said. Whether the direction of the first hour of the session (9:30 to 10:30 New York) goes with the direction of the rest of the session after it.
turns.if_asked: SPY. First hour up or down against the rest of the day up or down.

turns.text: How far does QQQ usually bounce after a bad open?
turns.intent: QQQ: on days that start badly, how far the price typically comes back up. 'A bad open' has no size and could be a gap down or a weak first stretch, so the reading has to be said or asked; no size may be invented.
turns.if_asked: A gap down of at least half a percent at the open; the bounce is from the low of the first half hour to the day's high after it.
turns.also_fine: Answering with a stated reading that invents no number: for example days QQQ opened below the previous close (any size), and how far it rose from the open to the day's high.

turns.intent: As a first message: no ticker named, so the default (SPY), said. Whether Fridays behave differently from the other weekdays (the day's move by weekday, Friday set against the rest).
turns.if_asked: SPY, how Fridays compare with the other days of the week.
turns.also_fine: Asking 'different in what' is acceptable only if the comparison by weekday is offered as the default.

turns.text: Does SPY tend to reverse during lunch?
turns.intent: SPY: whether the direction of the morning tends to turn around over the lunch hours (roughly 11:30 to 13:30 New York).
turns.if_asked: Whatever it did from the open until lunch, does it go the other way between about 11:30 and 1:30 New York time.
turns.also_fine: Asking which hours 'lunch' means, or what move is being reversed, is acceptable if it is one short question.

turns.text: What happens after three consecutive down days?
turns.intent: No ticker named, so the default (SPY), said. On the session after three or more sessions in a row that closed down, what the price typically did.
turns.if_asked: SPY, the day after three down closes in a row.
turns.also_fine: Exactly three in a row instead of three or more, if said.

turns.text: How often does the market take out yesterday's high?
turns.intent: 'The market' with no ticker: the default (SPY), said. How often the price trades above the previous session's high at some point during the session.
turns.if_asked: SPY, trading above the previous day's high at any time in the day.

turns.intent: Deliberately incomplete: bounce after what, and over what period, is not said. The assistant must ask what event or period is meant and must not invent a condition.
turns.if_asked: After it falls 1% from the open in the morning, does it close above where it was at noon.

turns.text: buy spy puts at 10am after a 1% up day, sell at 3pm
turns.intent: Backtest: buy SPY puts (same-day expiration and the strike are not stated, so the defaults, said) at 10:00 New York time on days after SPY closed up 1% or more, sell at 15:00 New York time.
turns.if_asked: New York time. At-the-money, same-day expiration, one contract.

turns.text: What if I bought calls instead?
turns.intent: The same backtest with calls instead of puts; everything else unchanged.

turns.text: What if I risked $200 and exited an hour later?
turns.intent: The same call backtest, sized so that each trade risks $200, and with the exit moved one hour later than it was (16:00 New York, the close).
turns.if_asked: Risk $200 a trade. An hour later than the 3pm exit, so at the close.
turns.also_fine: Reading 'an hour later' as one hour after the entry, if that is said or asked about.

turns.text: Buy ATM SPY 0DTE calls at 7am, out by 1245 PST, sell when they're up 40%
turns.intent: Backtest: buy at-the-money same-day SPY calls at 7:00 Pacific (10:00 New York); sell when the calls' price is up 40% from what was paid; otherwise close by 12:45 Pacific (15:45 New York). 1245 is a clock time, and 40% is of the option's price, not of SPY's.
turns.if_asked: Pacific time for both. 40% on the option premium.

turns.text: When does IWM put in its high?
turns.intent: IWM: at what time of day the session's high is usually made. 'Put in' is a verb here; no option is involved.
turns.if_asked: The time of day of IWM's daily high.

turns.text: Does SPY close above its 7 AM Pacific price on days after it fell at least 1%?
turns.intent: SPY: how often the close is above the price at 7:00 Pacific (10:00 New York), only on days following a decline of at least 1% (previous close to close).
turns.if_asked: 7 AM Pacific is 10 AM New York. The 1% decline is the previous day's close-to-close move.
